Description: Mingle with fellow makers to craft, chat, and unwind with snacks and good company. Try your hand at creating your own junk journal! | $20.00

Title: Rooted in Community: Craft Together, Oct 21 ~ Coverdale Farm Preserve
Description: Craving creativity? Tired of crafting alone? Mingle fellow makers to spark ideas in a fun, welcoming space. Bring a project—or just yourself! Whether expert or beginner, come craft, chat, and unwind with snacks and good company | $7.00

Title: Beatrix Potter’s Botanical Lecture & Book Signing at UD Botanic Gardens
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Classes; Free; Lectures & Workshops; Schools & Universities
Description: Among Beatrix Potter’s many accomplishments, she produced exquisite renderings of flowers and detailed botanical illustrations. The lecture showcases her work and explores the various plants and their influence in her life, gardens, and beloved children’s books. Whether you are a lover of plants, Peter Rabbit, or Potter herself, you find something to appreciate in her art of flora and fungi. Marta McDowell teaches landscape history and horticulture at the New York Botanical Garden and is a popular lecturer and writer. The recent publication of Beatrix Potter’s Botanical follows her 2023 book Gardening Can Be Murder, which explores the horticultural connections to crime fiction. Timber Press also published Unearthing The Secret Garden, Emily Dickinson's Gardening Life, The World of Laura Ingalls Wilder, New York Times-bestselling All the Presidents' Gardens, and Beatrix Potter’s Gardening Life, now in its ninth printing. She was the 2019 recipient of the Garden Club of America's Sarah Chapman Francis Medal for outstanding literary achievement. If you need a reasonable accommodation or for inquiries about accessibility, please contact Emily Mox at emox@udel.edu or 302-831-4188. All reasonable accommodation requests should be made at least two weeks prior to the event. Cancellation Policy: UDBG reserves the right to cancel any program if necessary. Refunds take approximately 3-4 weeks to process. There will be no refunds after a class or series has begun. Payment will be refunded if cancellation is made 10 days prior to the event.

Title: Intro to Japanese Stab Binding
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Join local artist Katie LeCocq in making your own hand sewn journal or sketchbook. We will repurpose a variety of paper to build your custom book bound in the Japanese Stab Binding style using items you likely have around your home. Additional $8 material fee. Ages 18+

Title: Grow Your Garden for Less with Seed Collecting
Description: Harvesting seeds is one of the most cost-efficient and rewarding ways to expand your garden. In this hands-on workshop, you will master the best techniques for collecting, cleaning, and storing seeds produced by native trees, shrubs, and perennials. In this class, you can expect: Guided by an Expert Conservator: The session begins with a lecture led by Lindsey Laban, Mt. Cuba Center’s Conservation Propagator. Lindsey spends her days propagating plants for Mt. Cuba’s gardens, natural lands, and elite conservation partners. Hands-on in the Gardens: Following the lecture, you will head out into Mt. Cuba’s living collections for an interactive seed-collecting session. Under Lindsey’s expert guidance, you will practice proper harvesting techniques firsthand. Take the Gardens Home: You will leave the workshop not only with newfound confidence, but also with a diverse array of hand-collected seed samples sourced directly from Mt. Cuba’s gardens, ready to transform your own backyard. This program takes place in-person at Mt. Cuba Center Thursday, October 22, 2026 (Rain Date: Thursday, October 29). 🥬 Certificate of Attendance for Continuing Education Units (CEUs) available 🥬 Gift or take home About the Instructor: Lindsey Laban is the Conservation Propagator at Mt. Cuba Center where she propagates plants for Mt.…

Title: Conservation Clinic
Organization: The Henry Francis du Pont Winterthur Museum, Inc.
Description: Bring in cherished objects and learn how to preserve them for future generations. From family quilts and photo albums to ceramics, portraits, furniture, and everything in between, conservation staff and students will hear the stories of your objects and share condition assessments, treatment recommendations, and display and storage advice. Your advance registration allows us to match you with someone who specializes in conservation of your object, whether it is a painting, textile, works of art on paper, book, archival document, photograph, furniture, or three-dimensional object (glass, ceramics, metals, organics). Free. By appointment only. Call 800.448.3883, x7029 to make an appointment. Limit three objects of the same media per 30-minute appointment. No monetary appraisals given. Conservation Clinics are also offered on December 10, 2026 and March 4 and April 1, 2027 . Photo by Evan Krape

Description: Sip & Stroll through the zoo and visit with the animals at our family-friendly happy hour event. Title: Moonlit Owls: An Intro to Scratch Art Family Art Class
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: A Halloween-themed scratch art workshop for children and their caregivers, introducing the process of revealing hidden imagery through contrast and texture. Participants will create spooky owl designs by scratching into a dark surface to reveal luminous silver or gold beneath, like uncovering moonlight in the night sky. Guided instruction will cover simple composition, line work, and pattern-building, while leaving space for personal creativity and expression. Each owl can take on a unique personality… mysterious, whimsical, or watchful… set against a Halloween-inspired background. A hands-on class focused on detail, discovery, and the satisfying reveal of glowing metallic imagery. Additional $10 material fee. Ages 6-12 with caregiver.

Title: Seasonal Terrarium Workshop
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: In this creative, beginner-friendly class, you’ll learn how to design and assemble your very own living terrarium using glass containers, natural materials, and a variety of easy-care plants for a tiny landscape. We’ll guide you through every step-from plant selection and layering to care tips that will keep your tiny garden thriving. Additional $25 material fee; $20 if you bring your own container. Ages 18+

Title: HEDWIG AND THE ANGRY INCH
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Get ready to lift up your hands for the most electrifying event of the season! The Milton Theatre is thrilled to present the cult-classic rock musical, Hedwig and the Angry Inch. Experience the grit and glamour like never before. The intimate setting of the Milton Theatre puts you right in the middle of the “Angry Inch” tour. There isn’t a bad seat in the house to witness every sequin, every tear, and every soaring high note of Stephen Trask’s legendary score. This groundbreaking, Obie-winning off-Broadway smash also won multiple awards for its hit film adaptation and Broadway revival. In a powerhouse one-night-only concert, “internationally ignored song stylist” Hedwig Schmidt takes to the stage to smash the fourth wall and rock the house. Hedwig, an East German rock ’n’ roll goddess, happens to be the victim of a botched sex-change operation, which has left her with an “angry inch.” Hedwig (née Hansel) explains her story in the form of a rock gig/stand-up comedy routine, backed by a hard-rocking band called “The Angry Inch.” Through songs and monologues, Hedwig tells her story, which began in the former East Berlin, where she met Luther, an American GI who promised to take her to the States on the condition that she change her genitalia. After the bungled operation, Luther abandons Hedwig in a Kansas trailer park, where she turns to music and meets geeky Tommy Speck, whom she mentors and deeply loves. Tommy steals her songs and achieves rock star fame, casting Hedwig aside. Demanding redress, she has stalked Tommy’s world tour, performing in the shabby venue next to his stadium show. Through head-banging anthems and heartfelt rock ballads, Hedwig describes her life’s search for “The Origin of Love” and a reunion with her other half. It’s a rocking ride – funny, touching, and ultimately inspiring to anyone who feels life gave them an inch when they deserved a mile. Hedwig and the Angry Inch is presented by special arrangement with Broadway Licensing Global. (www.broadwaylicensing.com)

Title: Basic Stringing Bracelet
Description: A fun and beginner-friendly bracelet making class designed for ages 6 and up. In this one-hour workshop, students will create a custom strung bracelet using a variety of beads in different colors and styles.

Title: THE WIZ
Description: The Tony® Award-winning Best Musical that took the world by storm is back. THE WIZ returns “home” to stages across America in an all-new tour, direct from Broadway. The Baltimore Sun raves “Powerhouse performances. Stunning choreography. Visionary sets” and the Chicago Sun-Times proclaims THE WIZ is “An eye-popping and high-intensity revival!” This groundbreaking twist on The Wizard of Oz changed the face of Broadway—from its iconic score packed with soul, gospel, rock, and 70s funk to its stirring tale of Dorothy’s journey to find her place in a contemporary world. Everybody rejoice--this dynamite infusion of ballet, jazz, and modern pop brings a whole new groove to easing on down the road!

Title: Knee High Naturalists: Leaves are Falling ~ Ashland Nature Center
Description: All over Ashland, colorful leaves are dancing on the breeze. Come join and play! Discover the wonders of nature with your little one! Enjoy hands-on nature discovery outdoors with our Teacher Naturalists. | $15.00 (ages 3-5)*

Title: Pyle and the Pre-Raphaelites Curator’s Cut: Behind-the-Scenes Library Talk
Description: Join Katherine Feldkamp, Curatorial Associate and Curator of Pyle and the Pre-Raphaelites , and Rachael DiEleuterio, Librarian and Archivist, to see and discuss the books, photographs, and archival materials that almost made it into the exhibition.

Title: Boos & Brews
Description: Our annual Boos & Brews celebration is where history gets a little haunted! Join Historic Lewes for a fun evening of live music by Electric Velvet, tavern drinks, food trucks brought to you by La Pinkeria Taco and Uncle B’s BBQ , ghost stories and a costume contest that’s sure to raise some spirits. Gather your favorite friends and celebrate one of Lewes’ favorite Halloween traditions! $45 per ticket and one drink ticket included per ticket. This is a 21+ event and advanced ticket purchase are encouraged since this popular event typically sells out.

Title: Watercolor Open Studio
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Join us to paint, experiment, and create in a relaxed studio environment. Bring your current watercolor project or try your hand at our featured still life set up. A watercolor instructor will be on hand to offer feedback and suggestions. Open to all skill levels. No instruction, no agenda. Students are responsible for bringing their own materials. Ages 18+

Title: Michael Mayo Live at Christina
Description: Experience an unforgettable night with Grammy-nominated jazz vocalist Michael Mayo as he performs original music from his 2024 Album "Fly" Experience an extraordinary night of music with Grammy-nominated jazz vocalist Michael Mayo as he brings his celebrated album Fly to the stage at Christina Cultural Arts Center. Renowned for his breathtaking vocal range and innovative artistry, Michael delivers a performance that blends jazz, soul, R&B, and improvisation into an unforgettable live experience. Whether you're a lifelong jazz enthusiast or simply looking for an inspiring night out, this is a concert you won't want to miss. Join us for an evening of world-class musicianship, captivating original music, and the intimate atmosphere that makes every performance at CCAC special. Seats are limited; reserve your tickets today and prepare to soar with the music of Fly!

Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Design and create an ornament Using glass components such as stringers, noodles, and frits, each student will design and create an ornament that will be fused in a kiln. The finished piece will be returned to Artspace after kiln firing for the student to pick up. Learn more about instructor Marcie Tauber on her website or in her instructor video. Age 16+. Younger kids are also welcome with a parent. Parents are free unless they are also participating. All materials provided.

Title: Building America: Sandcasting
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Trades were crucial to constructing buildings in America before, during and after the Revolution. Our Building America programs include demonstrations and interpretation of trades. We will discuss the tools and techniques associated with sandcasting and conduct demonstrations to show how gears for a mill were made.

Title: Halloween at the Farm
Categories: Festivals & Special Events; Visual Arts; Free
Description: @ Join us for a spook-tacular day of fall fun at Coverdale! Come in costume and participate in our Halloween Parade at 11 AM and 2 PM, then hop on a hayride through the autumn farm landscape. Enjoy animal demonstrations/education sessions, learn about their products, play classic fall games, and let your creativity shine with seasonal crafts. There’s something for the whole family to enjoy—and a few surprises along the way! Some activities may have a nominal fee. Register Here Some activities require a nominal fee In 2026, DelNature marks the 50th anniversary of the Harvest Moon Festival with a series of four distinct festivities: the Fall Native Plant Sale, A Taste of Coverdale, Autumn at Abbott’s, and Halloween at the Farm. Through these events, the festival’s past and present converge, sustaining its role as a cherished autumn tradition. A Taste of Coverdale is our premier annual fundraising event that serves as a community celebration of the unique places and food of Coverdale Farm Preserve. Funds raised directly support the ongoing stewardship and preservation of Delaware Nature Society’s sites and programs. Add to calendar Google Calendar iCalendar Outlook 365 Outlook Live

Title: Witch Stained Glass Suncatcher
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Ready to conjure some color? In this workshop, you’ll step into the "cauldron" of stained-glass creation to craft a Witch Suncatcher that’s more charming than chilling. Cast a glow over your windows with a piece that celebrates the mystical and the macabre all year round. Learn the foundations of the Tiffany Style of stained glass. You will select glass and learn how to cut, grind, foil and solder your project. Additional $30 material fee. Ages 18+ Stained Glass Attendance Policy: We ask participants to arrive no later than 10:15am for their class. If a participant arrives later, we will ask that they reschedule. Please note that the class ends promptly at 2pm. If a participant does not finish their project: The participant can schedule a time to come back to finish the project during one of the next stained-glass classes. The instructor can send foil home with the participant and sell them a $20 soldering tool so they can finish the project at home.

Title: Science Saturday - Creepy Chemistry
Description: Make spooky potions and marvel in the magic of chemical reactions.

Title: Hand Built Ceramic Mugs
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Explore basic hand-building pottery techniques like slab, coil and pinching. Use these techniques to create your own functional mug. After the student has created their piece, the instructor will mark glaze color choice. Because pieces will need to be fired, participants will be notified when pieces are ready to be picked up. Materials are included in the cost of class. Ages 18+

Title: Kids' Woodworking Project: Build a Birdhouse
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Start with a piece of cedar wood and learn how to use hand tools to make a bird house In this woodworking workshop for kids (age 10+) you will make your own bird house. The journey to the final bird house will cover important aspects related to woodworking including safety, key tools, tips and tricks and give you some hands-on practice time before starting the actual project. Note: By signing up for this workshop you acknowledge that the children will be using tools including but not limited to screw drivers, hammers, hand saws, power drills, power sanders, and will apply glue and stain or colors. Personal protective equipment will be provided but it will be critical for the children to be able to follow instructions and safety rules. Learn more about instructor Ben Fuchs' work on his website. All materials provided.

Title: Museum of the Macabre
Description: @ Dare to discover the dark side of science at this adult-only evening of eerie exploration. Venue: The Otello Meucci Performing Arts Center at Newark Charter School
Description: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum is a musical with music and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim and book by Burt Shevelove and Larry Gelbart. Broadway's greatest farce is light, fast-paced, witty, irreverent and one of the funniest musicals ever written. A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum takes comedy back to its roots, combining situations from time-tested, 2000-year-old comedies of Roman playwright, Plautus, with the infectious energy of classic vaudeville. A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum is a nonstop laughfest in which Pseudolus, a crafty slave, struggles to win the hand of a beautiful, but slow-witted, courtesan named Philia for his young master, Hero, in exchange for freedom. The plot twists and turns with cases of mistaken identity, slamming doors and a showgirl or two. Title: DelArt Readers – Gabriele by Anne & Claire Berest
Description: Join us! The DelArt Readers, a community-led book club, meets monthly to discuss, debate, celebrate, and share both works of fiction and non-fiction. Our selections are focused on art, artists, and/or the artistic process either in general or in response to the Museum’s collections or exhibits. In addition to our interest in art and artists, we also seek to create a sense of community, conversation, and connection. Join us in-person at DelArt on October 29 for Gabriele by Anne & Claire Berest. Written by Gabriele Buffet’s great granddaughters, this novel tells the story of how Gabriele Buffet, Francis Picabia and Marcel Duchamp meet, fall in love, marry, change the art world and redefine avant-garde as they move between Paris, New York, Berlin, Zurich, Barcelona, London and Saint-Tropez. Title: Botanical Workshop: Lichens and Moss
Description: Beyond being the sole subject of your paintings and drawings, mosses, lichens, and liverworts can also add vital context to your representations of native plants in their environment. Fall is an ideal time to observe the woodland floor at its most intricate, where cushions of moss and miniature forests of lichens form a vibrant, living tapestry. This workshop is about learning how to look, to see, and to study the subtle beauty of these ancient organisms. Understanding them requires looking closely and long enough to comprehend their complex structures—the velvety texture of mosses, the branching geometry of lichens, and the brilliant color variations of foliose forms are the fine details that reward deep observation. To inspire your process, the instructor will share examples of both modern and historical uses of these organisms in botanical illustrations. The day begins with a guided morning walk on Mt. Cuba’s grounds to observe lichens and mosses within their natural habitats, examining how they cling to bark, blanket rocks, and carpet the soil. Studio study follows, using diverse, fresh specimens that you can handle, compare, and observe under magnification at your own pace. You’ll leave with a practiced eye for these miniature ecosystems, a deeper…

Title: Coco Montoya
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: "One of the most prodigious and gifted electric bluesmen on the planet...a deeply soulful singer and incendiary guitarist [with] a seemingly endless penchant for invention." –AllMusic "Smoking songs and heavy hitting guitar full of fire and passion...Montoya’s rough-edged voice is filled with feeling. Bluesy, powerful and unpredictable...[It]really gets the blood flowing." –Blues Music Magazine "Montoya is a show-stopper...heartfelt singing and merciless guitar with a wicked icy burn. He is one of the truly gifted blues artists of his generation." –Living Blues “’Just play what you feel, be real about it, and enjoy yourself.’ That’s what Albert Collins taught me,” says the award-winning guitar virtuoso and soul-deep singer Coco Montoya. The self-taught, left-handed Montoya mastered his craft under Collins’ tutelage. Incorporating lessons learned from his mentors, the iconic Collins (for whom he originally drummed), and UK legend John Mayall, Montoya puts his own stamp onto every song he performs. Since his first solo album in 1995 (which won him the Blues Music Award for Best New Artist), Montoya’s endlessly inventive guitar work and passionate, hard-hitting vocals have kept him at the top of the blues world. With his new Alligator Records album, Writing On The Wall (his sixth for the label), Montoya delivers what he is already calling one of the best records he’s ever made. For the very first time on Alligator, he decided to bring his road-tested band—noted keyboardist and songwriter Jeff Paris (Keb’ Mo’, Bill Withers), bassist Nathan Brown, and drummer Rena Beavers—into the studio with him. Between the camaraderie of the long-time bandmates and the sheer talent of all involved, the results have left Coco, in his words, “over the moon.” Produced by Grammy Award-winner Tony Braunagel (Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal) and co-produced by Jeff Paris, Writing On The Wall is a tour-de-force of memorable, hook-filled songs, sung with passion and fueled by equally memorable, top shelf musicianship. The 13 tracks include five written or co-written by Montoya.

The show will honor the songs and stories from this beloved record while also featuring music spanning Mary’s extraordinary career. The Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter hailed by the Associated Press as “one of the best of her generation.” Known for her "scintillating confessional" style and hits like "Mercy Now," Gauthier returns to the stage with her acclaimed eleventh album, Dark Enough to See the Stars. This latest work marks a powerful shift, balancing her signature depth with ten "sparkling jewels" of songcraft that traverse the landscape of both profound loss and the beacon of new love.

Title: Succession Planting
Description: Even in small garden spaces, you can boost diversity and seasonal interest through succession planting. Succession planting is the practice of designing a garden so that as one plant finishes its peak growth or bloom cycle, another is ready to step into the spotlight. By thoughtfully timing and layering your plants, you ensure continuous color, texture, and ecological benefits throughout the year rather than a single, fleeting burst of spring blooms. Designed for gardeners of all levels, this class focuses on how to build these layered, ecologically rich plantings using native species. In this class, you will come away with: A clear understanding of succession planting and how it works in home gardens. The growth habits, site preferences, and key characteristics of native plants. How native plants can be combined to create layered garden design. Succession planting strategies for increasing biodiversity in your garden spaces. This class includes a guided walk through the gardens with Leah. Take home a ready-to-use plant groupings list and a simple approach to designing more diverse, resilient garden beds. Register now to learn how to keep your garden evolving beautifully through every season. This program takes place in-person at Mt. Cuba Center Saturday, October 31,…

Title: ELF THE MUSICAL – MATINEE
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: A title known the world over, Elf The Musical is a must-produce holiday musical that can easily become an annual tradition for any theatre. Based on the cherished 2003 New Line Cinema hit, Elf features songs by Tony Award nominees Matthew Sklar (The Prom, The Wedding Singer) and Chad Beguelin (Disney’s Aladdin on Broadway), with a book by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan (Annie, The Producers, Hairspray) and Bob Martin (The Drowsy Chaperone). Buddy, a young orphan, mistakenly crawls into Santa’s bag of gifts and is transported to the North Pole. The would-be elf is raised, unaware that he is actually a human until his enormous size and poor toy-making abilities cause him to face the truth. With Santa’s permission, Buddy embarks on a journey to New York City to find his birth father and discover his true identity. Faced with the harsh realities that his father is on the naughty list and his half-brother doesn’t even believe in Santa, Buddy is determined to win over his new family and help New York remember the true meaning of Christmas. This modern-day holiday classic is sure to make everyone embrace their inner elf. After all, the best way to spread Christmas Cheer is singing loud for all to hear. Elf The Musical is presented through special arrangement with Musical Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com

Title: The McCartney Experience – Encore!
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: “You close your eyes…it’s Paul McCartney. You open them…IT’S STILL PAUL McCARTNEY!” –Tom Freston, Founder, MTV “…the best Beatles / Paul McCartney tribute band. Jed Duvall not only looks and plays but most importantly sounds just like Paul and his band is very well put together. The play list is made up of both the best of the Beatles as well as Paul’s solo iconic hits. If you are a Beatles fan the Speed of Sound is a must see!!!” Al Cieslak, “The Kirk McEwen Show” THE McCARTNEY EXPERIENCE is THE tribute to Sir Paul, and leader Jed Duvall is almost like seeing the real thing. Playing a variety of songs from the Liverpool Legend, including Beatles, Wings and solo hits, THE McCARTNEY EXPERIENCE combines a band of seasoned musicians who love all things Paul, with the dedication and drive to get it right!

Title: Voices Unveiled: Music in Poetry, Image and Dance
Categories: Classical / Opera; Dance; Free; Visual Arts
Description: Collaborative pianist Rebecca Wilt gathers a luminous ensemble of artists: sopranos Makeda Hampton and Elizabeth Joy Kelly, trumpeter Brianne Borden, dancer Ashley SK Davis, and oboist Rebecca Mindock. Together they bring to life, Voices Unveiled: Music in Poetry, Image, and Dance. In this evocative celebration of women in the arts, music becomes poetry, movement becomes image, and sound becomes a language all its own. Featuring works by living female composers and performed entirely by women from Delaware, Voices Unveiled shines a light on the extraordinary breadth, imagination, and expressive power of women as creators and interpreters. Together, these remarkable artists invite us to listen more deeply, see more vividly, and feel more profoundly; to discover the voices that have always been there, waiting to be heard. Voices Unveiled is a celebration of artistic courage, human connection, and the enduring power of women to shape the world through art.

Title: HEDWIG AND THE ANGRY INCH
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Get ready to lift up your hands for the most electrifying event of the season! The Milton Theatre is thrilled to present the cult-classic rock musical, Hedwig and the Angry Inch. Experience the grit and glamour like never before. The intimate setting of the Milton Theatre puts you right in the middle of the “Angry Inch” tour. There isn’t a bad seat in the house to witness every sequin, every tear, and every soaring high note of Stephen Trask’s legendary score. This groundbreaking, Obie-winning off-Broadway smash also won multiple awards for its hit film adaptation and Broadway revival. In a powerhouse one-night-only concert, “internationally ignored song stylist” Hedwig Schmidt takes to the stage to smash the fourth wall and rock the house. Hedwig, an East German rock ’n’ roll goddess, happens to be the victim of a botched sex-change operation, which has left her with an “angry inch.” Hedwig (née Hansel) explains her story in the form of a rock gig/stand-up comedy routine, backed by a hard-rocking band called “The Angry Inch.” Through songs and monologues, Hedwig tells her story, which began in the former East Berlin, where she met Luther, an American GI who promised to take her to the States on the condition that she change her genitalia. After the bungled operation, Luther abandons Hedwig in a Kansas trailer park, where she turns to music and meets geeky Tommy Speck, whom she mentors and deeply loves. Tommy steals her songs and achieves rock star fame, casting Hedwig aside. Demanding redress, she has stalked Tommy’s world tour, performing in the shabby venue next to his stadium show. Through head-banging anthems and heartfelt rock ballads, Hedwig describes her life’s search for “The Origin of Love” and a reunion with her other half. It’s a rocking ride – funny, touching, and ultimately inspiring to anyone who feels life gave them an inch when they deserved a mile. Hedwig and the Angry Inch is presented by special arrangement with Broadway Licensing Global. (www.broadwaylicensing.com)

Title: The Sensory Studio: Creative Exploration
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: The Sensory Studio: Creative Exploration is a neurodivergent-friendly creative environment designed for exploration, regulation, and expressive making without pressure or expectation. This open studio experience offers a variety of art materials, such as clay, paint, drawing tools, collage, and tactile sensory elements… inviting children to engage in whatever way feels most comfortable for their bodies and nervous systems. Rather than following a single required project, students are offered gentle invitations and optional creative prompts alongside completely open-ended making time. Some children may choose to follow a simple guided idea, while others may prefer to experiment freely, focus on sensory engagement, or move between materials at their own pace. This class honors different communication styles, attention needs, and sensory experiences. The emphasis is not on finished artwork, but on process, comfort, and creative self-expression. Additional $10 material fee. Ages 5-12 with caregiver.

Title: Tuesday Creators' Club — November
Description: Weekly sessions November 3, 10, 17, & 24. Designed for artists ages 7–13, this class features a new theme and instructor each month, giving young creators the opportunity to explore a wide variety of artistic styles, techniques, and materials. November Theme: Coming Soon!

Title: Beyond Beginner’s Watercolor
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Explore the use of light, shadow and color to create forms using watercolors. Previous experience required. Additional $30 material fee. Ages 18+. Wednesdays 11/4/2026 - 12/4/2026

Title: Homeschooling Art Days
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Step into a world where creativity opens portals to wonder! In this imaginative art class, students will explore the lives and works of famous artists, dive into vibrant cultures through their art, and experiment with techniques that stretch across time and place. Each week offers hands-on projects that blend art history, storytelling, and self-expression—inviting kids to reinterpret masterpieces, try new methods, and make magic of their own. From swirling brushstrokes to ancient patterns, this is a journey where art becomes alive, and every child is part of the story. Additional $20 material fee. Ages 6-14. Wednesdays 11/4/2026 - 12/2/2026

Title: Open Studio: Drawing & Painting
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Unlock your full artistic potential with artist and artist-educator, Jen Polillo. Join fellow art makers and become part of this supportive open studio community! With Jen’s coaching and mentorship, you will: establish a structured weekly practice, receive individualized guidance, create amongst your peers in the drawing & painting studio, set and reach your goals and be a part of an uplifting artist community. Bring your supplies and a project you're working on, work from a multitude of still-life set-ups in the studio or explore the materials we have on hand to get the inspiration flowing. Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced artists are all welcome! Ages 18+ Wednesdays 11/4/2026 - 12/23/2026

Title: Improv for Everyone
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Ever wondered what it takes to improvise on stage? This energetic 6-week series gets you performance-ready, building the skills and confidence to shine in front of an audience. Improv for Everyone is built for anyone ready to step into the spotlight or who wants the everyday benefits it teaches. In a high-energy, supportive environment, you'll learn the core techniques of improvisation while developing the tools every performer needs, including: - Confidence commanding the stage - Listening closely and staying present in the moment - Quick, creative thinking on the spot - Communication that feels natural rather than forced - Working well with others in a supportive setting Whether you're dreaming of joining a troupe, improving your comedic chops, meeting new people, or just enjoy two fun-filled hours a week of laughter and play — whatever brings you, we can't wait for you to join us! Title: Knee High in the Kitchen, Nov 4 ~ Coverdale Farm Preserve
Description: Preschoolers and their grown-ups enjoy a hands-on cooking class using simple, fresh ingredients. Together they mix, measure, and taste, building early skills and confidence. Each session ends with a tasty snack they make side-by-side. | $25.00 (ages 3-5)*

Title: Appreciating Natural Night (Online)
Categories: Literature & Poetry; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Gardening often focuses on sunlight as essential for growth, but darkness is also required for gardens (and gardeners) to truly thrive. In this talk, Leigh Ann Henion will share how spending time with synchronous fireflies motivated her to explore the importance of natural darkness in an age of increasing artificial light. Drawing from her celebrated book, Night Magic: Adventures Among Glowworms, Moon Gardens, and Other Marvels of the Dark, Henion will offer inspiring stories and empowering guidance about how embracing the night can lead to moments of wonder, reduced light pollution, and improved ecological health. Take part in our flexible online learning offerings. Join live to participate in our online learning community or watch after as your schedule allows. All registrants will receive a recording of the class with access to view the class for 30 days after the live session This program takes place online Wednesday, November 4, 2026. 🥬 New class 🥬 Online About the Instructor: Leigh Ann Henion is the New York Times bestselling author of Phenomenal and Night Magic: Adventures Among Glowworms, Moon Gardens, and Other Marvels of the Dark. Title: Furniture Painting 101
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Learn the basics of transforming furniture with Fusion Mineral Paint, from proper prep to beautiful finishing techniques. Together, we'll paint an instructor-led furniture piece, then you'll create your own small wood project to take home. Topics include surface preparation, achieving a smooth brushstroke-free finish, applying topcoats, and adding finishing touches. Material fee includes your project, a 2-ounce paint sample, and a brush to keep. Perfect for beginners looking to refresh their home with creativity and confidence! If you are interested in a specific Fusion Mineral Paint color email the instructor, Sue Walton at bvintage813@gmail.com. Additional $25 material fee. *Take-home projects are typically a tray or sign and are subject to availability. Actual projects may vary from those pictured. Ages 18+

Title: Gilmore Girls Mug Paint Party
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: A cozy, nostalgia-filled mug painting workshop for adults, inspired by the warmth, humor, and iconic details of a beloved small-town series. Participants will paint pre-fired ceramic mugs featuring subtle references, inside jokes, and character-inspired motifs drawn from the show’s most lovable moments. From coffee-filled charm to witty nods only true fans will recognize, each mug becomes a personal keepsake layered with meaning and memory. A relaxed, creative evening focused on storytelling through design, community, and the comfort of making something both functional and deeply nostalgic. Additional $15 material fee. Ages 18+

Title: Beginner Drawing with Pen and Ink
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Discover the expressive power of the dip pen-an ancient drawing tool that continues to inspire artists today. In this workshop, artists will learn essential tips and techniques to create dynamic, fluid, and detailed drawings using dip pens and ink. Through guided exercises and hands-on practice, you'll explore line variation, texture, cross-hatching, and mark-making to develop your own visual language. All levels welcome. Additional $10 material fee. Ages 18+

Title: Processing in the Revolution: The Madison Factory and Merino Mania
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Learn how the craze for fine Merino wool gave rise to the American textile revolution. Discover how a sheep changed America’s history. Explore both the origins of the Madison Factory and the machinery that made woolen cloth in the Early Republic. We will follow our presentation with a tour of the Madison Factory.

Description: In this class, participants will discuss various techniques for effectively painting a landscape, inspired by the beautiful Mt. Cuba gardens, while the instructor will provide one-on-one instruction for participating students. Lessons on composition and color mixing will be covered. Knowledge of drawing and painting is required, but experience with oils is not necessary. Participants are welcome to “plein air” paint on the grounds. The class will be held on Thursday 11/5 virtually 7 – 9 pm, then two in-person Saturdays 11/7 and 11/14, 10 am – 4 pm at Mt. Cuba Center. Please bring your lunch when onsite. Title: Research at Winterthur Speaker Series
Organization: The Henry Francis du Pont Winterthur Museum, Inc.
Description: Unraveling ‘The Cause of Much Chagrin’: Multidisciplinary Approaches to Historic Shark and Ray Exploitation through Marine Shagreen Museum Objects Dr. Rachel M. Winter will speak about her ongoing research into identifying the seas and species exploited to produce marine shagreen using nearly two dozen objects in Winterthur’s collections she studied in consultation with Winterthur scientists, conservators, and curators. Dr. Winter’s project “‘The Cause of Much Chagrin’: Marine Shagreen as a Tool for Elasmobranch Historical Ecology,” was funded by a National Endowment for the Humanities Postdoctoral Fellowship at Winterthur in 2025. The Research at Winterthur series, presented by the Library, Research Fellowship Program, and Continuing Education, showcases new projects and publications that tap into our rich collections and resources, unveiling innovative perspectives for exploring the fascinating stories that objects can tell about people and our shared past. Registration required. Included with admission. Members free. Register now.

Title: JESSE GARRON’S TRIBUTE TO ELVIS – MATINEE
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: THE CLOSEST THING TO THE KING! Jesse Garron’s Tribute to Elvis is ranked among the most respected acts in local and nationwide venues. Acclaimed as “The “Closest Thing to the King,” Garron has been performing his Tribute since 1997. Garron possesses the voice, looks, and charisma that made Elvis a superstar and draws audiences in from the minute he walks on stage. Jesse, backed by live musicians and female vocalists, performs songs that cross three generations of rock, pop, gospel, and oldies music, so the act has universal appeal.

Title: Fused Glass Snowflakes
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Capture the intricate beauty of a winter flurry without the frostbite! In this specialized workshop, you’ll explore the "anatomy" of a snowflake through the medium of kiln-fired glass. Because no two snowflakes are alike in nature, this class encourages total geometric freedom and creative experimentation. Each student will make 1 snowflake. Pieces will need to be fused in a kiln. Students will be notified when pieces are ready for pick up. Additional $30 material fee. Ages 18+

Title: Stranger Sculptures Family Art Class
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: A special sculptural workshop inspired by Stranger Things Day, where participants create their own monster designs based on the mysterious creatures from the Upside Down. Using clay and sculptural materials, students will explore form, texture, and imagination to build their own original monster creations inspired by the eerie world of the show. Guided instruction will focus on beginner-friendly sculpting techniques, while leaving room for creative interpretation, character design, and personal expression. A hands-on, imagination-driven workshop where the strange and unknown take shape in clay! Additional $10 material fee. Ages 6-12 with caregiver.

Title: Historic Lewes First Friday Community Nights
Description: Experience a taste of what Historic Lewes has to offer our community on First Fridays! Each month from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m., visit the Sussex Tavern for a colonial-inspired beverage, stop into the Lewistown Coffee-house for a taste of the Revolution, browse the Historic Lewes Antique Shop, listen to live music, take a tour, and enjoy stories from bygone times…all in the beautiful setting of our Historic Lewes Town Campus. Title: Watercolor Open Studio
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Join us to paint, experiment, and create in a relaxed studio environment. Bring your current watercolor project or try your hand at our featured still life set up. A watercolor instructor will be on hand to offer feedback and suggestions. Open to all skill levels. No instruction, no agenda. Students are responsible for bringing their own materials. Ages 18+

Title: Purple Piano - The One-Man Tribute to Prince
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Since 2011, Marshall Charloff has established his dominance as the world’s leading Prince Tribute Artist. Coming from fronting the greatest Prince tribute show in the world, working with the Atlanta Rhythm Section and writing and producing the Commodores, Marshall has now embarked on a solo journey, performing all of your favorite Prince songs as the one-man show — “PURPLE PIANO”. Minneapolis native Marshall was raised in the epicenter of 1980’s music production, and cut his musical teeth working with SuperProducers John Fields and Steven “Funkytown” Greenberg. At age 19, Marshall, like Prince, was discovered and signed by producer Pepe Willie. Marshall is featured on 94 East albums with Prince, where he plays guitar and Prince is on vocals. Marshall has performed worldwide- fronting the finest symphonies in most major cities in North America, featuring the music of Prince; and continues to tour fronting the celebrated Purple xPeRieNCE. $37 VIP | $34 Balcony | $30 General Admission Doors open 45 minutes prior to show *Does not include convenience or handling fees* No refunds or exchanges

Title: Gelli Printmaking
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Gelli printing is a form of monoprinting with a flexible silicone plate, using stencils, textures, and layering. Gelli printing is a form of mono-printing that uses a flexible silicone plate to create unique and expressive prints. By applying paint to the plate and using various tools and techniques, you can achieve surprising and unpredictable results, making each print a one-of-a-kind creation. In this three-hour hands-on class, we will guide you through demonstrations and provide expert tips and tricks. Then, it's your turn to experiment! You'll have ample time to create unique prints using textures, masks, and layering techniques. No prior experience is necessary – bring your enthusiasm and a willingness to experiment. Learn more about instructor Susan Benarcik on her website. Age 16+. All materials provided.

Title: Glow of Fall
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Make a glowing leaf lantern using translucent materials and real leaves while exploring light and color. A calm, cozy class with soft sensory elements and a peaceful mindfulness moment. Additional $5 material fee. Ages 4–8 (flexible + sibling-friendly)

Title: Genealogist in Residence
Description: Gather your materials, gather your thoughts, and come see us on the first Saturday of each month with the exception of January from 10:00 AM. to 1:00 P.M. for the Genealogist in Residence Program. Members of the Sussex County Genealogical Society, including Historic Lewes member and volunteer Iris Fisher, will be available to help anyone that has a question about their family tree. The member-experts are seasoned searchers who come from different areas and are ready to help answer your questions regardless of what corner of the globe your quest may lead you! As an added benefit the Historic Lewes archives’ family files will be available for your use. The Genealogist in Residence program is sponsored by the Lewes Historical Society and the Sussex County Genealogical Society.

Title: Clay Happy Lil’ Candy Corn Dish Family Art Class
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: A gentle clay experience for toddlers and their caregivers, where little hands help create a cheerful candy corn dish. Children will explore soft clay through touch, pressing, and shaping while caregivers assist in forming a small pinch-pot style dish. Simple decorating and texture tools will be used to add playful candy corn colors and patterns. Each piece becomes a bright, happy seasonal keepsake made together. A calm, playful studio space where tiny makers can enjoy their clay creations! Additional $10 material fee. Ages 12 months-5 with caregiver.

Title: Stranger Sculptures
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: A creature sculpture workshop for children, where participants create clay interpretations of Demogorgons or Demodogs inspired by a mysterious alternate world of monsters and shadows. Students will explore beginner-friendly sculpting techniques including shaping, building form, adding texture, and creating expressive features as they bring their chosen creature to life. Guidance will be provided throughout, while still allowing space for personal interpretation, exaggeration, and imaginative detail. A hands-on, monster-making experience focused on creativity, texture, and sculptural storytelling in a fun and immersive studio environment! Additional $10 material fee. Ages 6-12.

Title: Connecting Generations: Make Your Own Bowl
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Try something new and experience art with your family and friends. Create your own wheel thrown bowl from start to finish while enjoying time together. Learn the basics of the potter’s wheel from centering to forming in this fun and encouraging environment. Our skilled instructor will be there to help every step of the way. After the student has created their piece, the instructor will mark glaze color choice. Materials are included in the cost of class. Because pieces will need to be fired, participants will be notified when pieces are ready to be picked up. Adults and ages 12+ with a caregiver.

Description: A detail and result oriented class that will go over how to produce the forms and figures used in carving faces in wood. We will go over the safety of wood carving, as well as the simple shapes that become complex forms. We will be creating a finished piece in class. Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 1-3pm Ages: 16+ Instructor: Gabriel Hurd Cost: $75 Registration closes 24 hours prior. Title: Advanced Techniques with Alcohol Inks
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Local artist Nina Yocom will guide students on more in-depth techniques for working with alcohol inks Students will learn how to use different drying tools including hot, warm, and cool air flow to manipulate the inks on synthetic paper. She will work with students hands-on to create layered effects and how to work with stencils, acrylic painters and fine liner pens to create mixed media pieces. Finally, she will review how to reproduce alcohol ink designs as greeting cards, wall hangings, mugs, magnets and more, as well as ways to frame finished paintings. Learn more about Nina on her website. All materials included. Ages 16+.

Title: Princess Sing-A-Long
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Kids & Family Friendly; Music; Theater & Performance
Description: Experience the magic and music of 10 royal princesses! This is a live performance packed with your favorite family-friends' songs and characters. Title: Singer-Songwriter Showcase
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Strip away the over-production and get straight to the soul of the music. Join us at the historic Milton Theatre for an exclusive Singer-Songwriter Showcase , a night dedicated to the raw, authentic voices of the Delmarva Peninsula. From the stories behind the lyrics to the melodies that define our region, this is your chance to experience local talent in its purest form. Whether you love folk, country, rock, or soul, you’ll discover your new favorite artist in our intimate venue. Don’t miss this celebration of the incredible creativity right in our backyard. Sol Knopf is an award winning singer/songwriter and solo performer from the state of Delaware in the USA. He is a 2022 inductee into the Delaware Rock n Roll Society’s Hall of Fame. Sol is best known for his distinctive baritone voice and timeless original songs. His moving single “My Baby Girl” (co-written with Geri Smith) became one of the most requested, independently released, father/daughter dance songs across the USA and abroad in 2016. Ed Shockley has been making music professionally since he was barely a teenager. He has spent his adult life writing and recording music with bands as a lead vocalist and drummer. At the same time, Ed has recorded and performed live, supporting dozens and dozens of talented artists. Keith Mack is a celebrated rock guitarist who has backed many of music’s iconic voices over the last 40 years. After years of playing with Patty Smyth, Joe Cocker, Paul Young, Cyndi Lauper and others

Title: Tavern Night 2026
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Tavern Night is a one-of-a-kind evening of 18th-century-inspired food, drink, music, and live auction. Participants will enjoy the warmth of the fire as they delight in a selection of flavors and aromas representative of those found in a colonial tavern. Title: Paint Your Pet
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Venue: Gilbert W. Perry Center for the Arts (The Gibby)
Description: Create a custom portrait of your beloved pet in this beginner friendly acrylic painting workshop. Participants will submit a photo of their pet prior to class, and a sketch will be prepared on canvas before the event. Students will learn color mixing, fur textures, highlights, and painting techniques while creating a keepsake portrait to take home. Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 6:00 - 8:30 pm Ages: 16+ Instructor: Christin Smietka Cost: $55 Registration Closes three-days prior. Title: The Great American Songbook Cabaret
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Join us for “The Great American Songbook Cabaret,” where the golden age of American music returns to life on the Milton Theatre stage! From the sophisticated melodies of Cole Porter to the soulful tunes of George Gershwin, experience the music that has defined generations and inspired a nation. This is more than a concert—it’s a cabaret celebration. Our handpicked ensemble, led by Director and Vocalist Candice Castro and including the incredible talents of Erin Bobby, Jordan Kilgore, and Matt Lucatamo, will deliver powerful, fresh, and unforgettable interpretations of these legendary hits. Supported by a live pit band under the guidance of Steven Soltow, every song will be an experience in itself.

Title: Susan Werner with Heather Maloney
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Acclaimed singer-songwriter Susan Werner brings her witty lyrics, masterful musicianship, and genre-defying style to Arden Gild Hall on November 7, 2026. Blending folk, jazz, blues, Americana, and sharp storytelling, Werner has earned a national following for her captivating live performances and intelligent, heartfelt songs. Don't miss an evening with one of America's most original and engaging musical voices. Massachusetts-based “writer song-singer” Heather Maloney found music in the midst of three years at a meditation center, honing a sound moored in days of silent reflection and reverence for storytellers like Joni, Rilke, Ken Burns, and the anonymous authors of Zen parables. While she eventually traded the quiet, structured life of a yogi for the kinetic life of a touring musician, the core of her songwriting has remained centered around same curiosity about our inner world and the desire to articulate it through storytelling.

Title: Modern Love Debut, Phase I
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Elissa Davis of Elissa Davis Art.com is debuting her painting series, Modern Love ! The series of paintings explores how certain qualities can be embodied and expressed through our intentions and actions in modern times. The six qualities are gentleness, gratitude, determination, kindness, intentional. and joyful. Each quality is painted as a figure and presented within a diverse cultural, gendered, racial, multigenerational and abled lens of representation. Modern Love is a two-year series and will debut Phase I on; Sunday, November 8th, 2026, 2:00-4:00 Delaware Center for Horticulture, Wilmington, Delaware. All are welcome to attend at no charge!

Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Participants will create a stunning botanical painting using watercolor, ink, and metal leaf based on local artist Katie LeCocq’s series “Heart of Gold.” A wildflower sketch will be provided to start things off, but artists are welcome to start from scratch and bring their own botanical inspiration. We will first watercolor our paintings. In the next session, we will use a dip pen and ink to incorporate details, and in the final session, artists will choose between gold, silver and copper for their final metal leaf element. Title: Tarkus – Tribute to Emerson, Lake & Palmer
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: We are dedicated to celebrating the compositional genius and groundbreaking work of this iconic trio. Keith Turner grew up playing piano in the golden age of R & B, Classic Rock, and Motown,the 60’s & 70’s. He studied music at CCC while writing and performing originals and ELP for his class which included the late Billy Paul. Keith was ecstatic when asked to play in Tarkus. Keith Emerson was one of my earliest influences shall we say “From the Beginning! Mike is a well respected multi-instrumentalist out of the New Jersey/Philadelphia area. Coming from a musical family, Mike starting out drumming following in the footsteps of his older brother John. His father was an accomplished singer and front man, and Mike’s sister Karen plays piano. Music was always permeating throughout the household, including the music of Genesis, Yes, ELP, and The Beatles. Mike started guitar at age 11 and had formal lessons from jazz instructor Bill Johnson out of New Jersey. John started drumming at age 13. His influences include John Bonham, Carl Palmer, Dave Weckl and Buddy Rich among many others. He studied with local instructors and played in school bands as a teenager. After years of playing in area clubs, he moved out west to attend The Musicians Institute in Hollywood, CA where he graduated with honors. John toured the Vegas casino circuit and the world aboard cruise ships before returning to his native Delaware where he seeks challenging musical opportunities such as Tarkus.

Title: Little Hands Clay Studio
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Little Hands Clay Studio is a gentle, sensory-rich clay experience designed for children ages 3–6 and their caregivers. This class invites our youngest makers to explore clay through touch, texture, and simple foundational techniques in a calm, playful environment. Together, children and caregivers will be introduced to basic clay forms such as pinch pots, coils, and simple building methods, while also spending time freely exploring clay tools, textures, and movement. The focus is not on perfect outcomes, but on discovery, sensory engagement, and shared creative experience. At this age, learning happens through doing, repeating, squishing, pressing, and experimenting. This class honors that natural developmental stage by slowing things down and allowing space for curiosity, mess, and process-led making. Caregivers are encouraged to participate alongside their child, supporting connection, regulation, and shared joy in the tactile experience of clay. Additional $15 material fee. Ages 3-6 with caregiver.

Title: Tuesday Sketch Night: The Doctor
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)

Whether you sketch a lot or haven't picked up a pencil in years, this 2-hour event is a non-judgmental space to practice observation and creativity. Title: Owl Howl
Description: Many people have heard the haunting call of an owl, but few have ever been lucky enough to spot one in the wild. Mt. Cuba’s diverse landscapes, mature trees, and rolling topography provide the absolute perfect habitat for three of Delaware’s spectacular native species: the Barred, Great Horned, and Eastern Screech owl. Because winter is peak roosting season, this is your best chance of the year to glimpse these majestic birds of prey. You will get a rare opportunity to explore Mt. Cuba’s stunning landscapes under the cover of twilight and darkness. Equipped with provided flashlights and binoculars and guided by experts, you can expect: Expert Instruction: Begin with a brief, fascinating look into the secretive lives, silent flight adaptations, and behaviors of local owls. The Night Trek: Venture deep into the quiet areas of the gardens just after dusk. An Acoustic Hunt: Learn to identify distinct calls and use guided listening techniques to locate where these apex predators are actively roosting in the winter canopy. This immersive experience goes far beyond a typical nature walk. By learning to look at the night landscape through the eyes of an owl, you will leave with the knowledge and tools to: Confidently…

Title: 13: The Musical
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: 13: The Musical Book by Dan Elish & Robert Horn Music & Lyrics by Jason Robert Brown Directed by Matt Hatfield November 13 – 15, 2026 Being 13 is hard. But at least you can sing about it. The Clear Space Arts Institute Spotlight on Young Performers program is the perfect group to bring to life Tony Award winner Jason Robert Brown’s heartwarming and hilarious coming of age musical comedy to the stage. Evan Goldman is plucked from his home in New York City and dropped into small-town Indiana right before his Bar Mitzvah. Making new friends while navigating crushes, cliques, and rumors, Evan is like all of us once upon a time: growing up faster than we hoped while still trying to cling to the fun of just being a kid.

Title: Flifferschmeep, A Musical Comedy
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Venue: Laird Performing Arts Center at Tatnall School
Description: Profundo Bono, Delaware’s theater company composed entirely of judges, lawyers, and other legal professionals, will be performing its 11th musical comedy this year, Flifferschmeep, Another Example of What Happens When You Get Lawyers Involved, on November 13, 14, and 15, 2026 in Wilmington at the Laird Performing Arts Center at Tatnall School (13th & 14th) and in Dover at a location to be determined (15th). What is “Flifferschmeep,” you ask? I’m glad you asked. It’s two things: Flifferschmeep, Another Example of What Happens When You Get Lawyers Involved, is an original musical comedy by Lyons McBean, adapted from the author’s novel of the same name—which he is desperately trying to self-publish. The production features: 30 characters played by 26 actors 25 unoriginal musical numbers At least one cameo appearance A steadily escalating sequence of events that becomes increasingly difficult to explain Performances will take place: November 13 and 14 in Wilmington November 15 in Dover But what does Flifferschmeep mean? It’s something literally earth-changing — but to know the answer, you need to come to the show.

Title: Jester Presents: Studio Concert with Sharon Bousquet
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Singer-songwriter Sharon Bousquet brings her original Soulful Folk & Acoustic Fingerstyle Covers to Jester Artspace. Wilmington-based musician Sharon Bousquet creates soulful folk and Americana music that spans decades of experience in an artful presentation both emotive and filled with intimate moments of connection and joy. Bousquet was the band leader of regional vocal trio The Sugar Maples: Erin, Sharon & Sky. Now working solo and in duo formats in Delaware and beyond, Sharon has expanded her original music with an array of carefully chosen cover songs that accent her deep skill on the acoustic guitar and powerhouse voice. With Joni Mitchell and Michael Hedges as primary influences, a house concert by Sharon Bousquet promises musicianship, presence, award-winning songwriting and the opportunity to create community around art and music. Title: Destination Soultown Feat. The Sensational Soul Cruisers
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Under the tutelage of legendary Jersey Shore saxophonist Screamin’ Steve Barlotta, The Sensational Soul Cruisers bring to you their Destination Soultown Show. This Concert focuses on iconic Classic Soul & Motown music from the period of time generally between the birth of Motown in 1960 to the release of Michael Jackson’s all-time selling Thriller Album in 1983. Joined by 11 performers including a horn section, keyboardists, 4 vocalists and an incredible Rock & Soul rhythm section, the Destination Soultown Experience recreates a note for note and absolutely live choreographed duplication of these classic tunes, from the early pioneers of Motown, Stax Records, Carolina Beach Music and The Sound of Philadelphia. Sprinkled throughout the show you will hear the sounds of artists like: Four Tops, Temptations, Jackson 5, Smokey Robinson, Sly and the Family Stone, The Spinners, Earth Wind & Fire, Edwin Starr, Sam & Dave, Carl Carton, Otis Redding, The Delfonics, Marvin Gaye, Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes, The Manhattans, Barry White, The Commodores, The Stylistics with many more soulful gems and surprises! The show touches on the crème de la crème of this vast catalogue from the Doo-Wop sounds of the Flamingos “I only have eyes for you” to very danceable “Ladies Night” by Kool and the Gang. With their multimedia video backdrop this show transcends generations making it one to be loved by all. Title: The Old State House Concert Series – Boxturtle Bob
Categories: Country / Folk / Bluegrass; Free; Kids & Family Friendly
Description: On Friday, November 13, Delaware Friends of Folk will present the next event in their 2026-27 Old State House concert series, inside the Old State House on The Green in Dover. This is the thirteenth season in the series which is produced in cooperation with the Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs and First State National Heritage Park and is supported by a generous grant from the Kent County Fund for the Arts. The one-hour performance will begin at 7:30 pm. The concert is free and open to the public. Doors open at 7:00 and seating is limited. The featured act is Cecil County performer Boxturtle Bob. Boxturtle Bob is a one-man band. He adeptly strums and picks his acoustic guitar while keeping the metronome-precise beat with his drum set and periodically playing zippy flourishes on his harmonica. His original songs make up a big portion of his set lists when performing at restaurants and bars in and around Cecil County, MD. His list of past and present bands includes the Crazy Planet Band, Nightstreet, Blues Blues, and Delmarva Folk Festival favorites, Planete Folle, which he described as a “cajun-zydeco version of the original Crazy Planet Band.“ In October 2025, Rob and the other members of the Crazy Planet Band were inducted into the Delaware Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. The Old State House concert series is presented by Delaware Friends of Folk. These events are supported by a grant from the Kent County Fund for the Arts, an organization that aims to enhance the quality of life, educate, and broaden perspectives by supporting the arts and arts organizations in Kent County. Support is also provided by the First State National Heritage Park, a partnership of State and City agencies under the leadership of Delaware State Parks and the Delaware Division of Historical and Cultural Affairs. Delaware Friends of Folk are partially supported by a grant from the Delaware Division of the Arts, a state agency, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. The Division promotes Delaware arts events on www.DelawareScene.com. Links: www.delfolk.org https://www.delfolk.org/state-house https://www.facebook.com/boxturtlebob.chirnside

Title: Holiday Magic: Metal Embossed Ornaments & Gift Tags
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Categories: Art Centers; Classes; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: Create embossed ornaments, gift tags, and garland from colorful metal. Relax, create, and take home unique décor! Create beautiful handcrafted decorations while discovering the art of metal embossing! In this fun, relaxing workshop, you'll transform copper-, gold-, and aluminum-tone metal sheets—made from both recycled and new roasting pans—into festive ornaments and decorative accents. Using simple embossing tools and techniques, you'll create three or more unique pieces that can be displayed as individual ornaments, strung together as a holiday garland, or used as elegant gift tags and card toppers. Choose from a large collection of patterns, including suns, moons, insects, cats, dogs, and seasonal designs, or bring your own artwork to personalize your creations. No previous experience is necessary. Metal embossing is an enjoyable, low-mess craft—just trace, emboss, and watch your designs come to life! All materials provided. Ages 13+. Title: Bundled & Unfiltered: Sweater Weather Comedy Show!
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Join us for a night where the knitwear is soft but the punchlines are sharp. As mid-November settles in, we’re bringing together the region’s funniest comedians to peel back the layers of holiday stress, family dynamics, and the struggle of surviving “cuffing season.” It’s the ultimate seasonal vibe: cozy enough for a first date, but honest enough to keep it real! Headliner: Don “Jream” Hines Don Hines AKA “JREAM” was blessed with the gift of comedy. As a young boy growing up in North Carolina, he would take his trials and tribulations and turn those experiences into laughter. He was always the center of attention, especially at family and friend gatherings. He always loved to make people laugh, especially his family. He used laughter as a means of bonding the family together particularly during times of struggles. The moment of truth came when he stepped out on faith in 2005. He entered the Tri-State talent show at Delaware State University. The competition was fierce and he was the only comedian to perform against a wide variety of incredible talent. It was in 2005 that he won first place, he has not stopped. Later in 2005 he gave his life to Christ and JREAM (Jesus Rules Everything Around Me) was born. Feature: Tim Conniff Tim Conniff is a stand up comedian known for his unique blend of clean comedy and a powerful message about stepping out of one’s comfort zone. He spent 30 years focused on his corporate career and family before rediscovering his passion for the stand up comedy stage. Tim transformed himself from a nervous first-timer to hosting comedy shows. Host: Keith Purnell Keith is one of the fastest rising comics from Delaware. He’s a high energy performer whose quick wit, style, and fast pace humor make him a hit and personal favorite of audiences young and old. He performs at Comedy Clubs across the country and has appeared on Television and in Movies. He was a winner in the Howard Stern “Kill or Be Killed” Comedy Competition and was the Philadelphia Regional winner in the Sierra Mist Next Great Comic Comedy Competition. Keith has had appearances on Last Comic Standing and is gaining a reputation as the next rising star.

Title: ELF THE MUSICAL
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: A title known the world over, Elf The Musical is a must-produce holiday musical that can easily become an annual tradition for any theatre. Based on the cherished 2003 New Line Cinema hit, Elf features songs by Tony Award nominees Matthew Sklar (The Prom, The Wedding Singer) and Chad Beguelin (Disney’s Aladdin on Broadway), with a book by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan (Annie, The Producers, Hairspray) and Bob Martin (The Drowsy Chaperone). Buddy, a young orphan, mistakenly crawls into Santa’s bag of gifts and is transported to the North Pole. The would-be elf is raised, unaware that he is actually a human until his enormous size and poor toy-making abilities cause him to face the truth. With Santa’s permission, Buddy embarks on a journey to New York City to find his birth father and discover his true identity. Faced with the harsh realities that his father is on the naughty list and his half-brother doesn’t even believe in Santa, Buddy is determined to win over his new family and help New York remember the true meaning of Christmas. This modern-day holiday classic is sure to make everyone embrace their inner elf. After all, the best way to spread Christmas Cheer is singing loud for all to hear. Title: Geoff Tate’s Operation: Mindcrime - The Final Chapter
Description: Multi-platinum selling, Grammy nominated singer/songwriter Geoff Tate is best known for his 30-plus years as the creative and driving force behind the progressive metal band Queensryche. Since its inception with Geoff at the helm, Queensryche has sold over 20 million albums worldwide and has performed in upwards of fifty countries. Geoff is regarded as one of the most skilled vocalists in the genre with hundreds of modern, popular artists citing him and his former band as a major influence. Combining social consciousness and expertly crafted lyrics with high-energy, melodically complex music, Queensryche with Geoff Tate at the forefront became internationally recognized as the thinking man's rock band. The band's first three albums -- their self-titled EP (1983), The Warning (1984) and Rage for Order (1986) -- all hit gold status selling over 500,000 units each. Beginning in March 2025, Geoff and the current line-up of Operation: Mindcrime, hit the road to celebrate the final chapter of Operation: Mindcrime, performing the 1988 landmark concept album from beginning to end in its entirety... It's a show that Geoff loves to perform and fans love to see, only proving that good music never goes out of style. As always, Geoff looks forward to the musical journey that lies ahead and can’t wait to perform his next big rock show.

Title: White Nights
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Before there was Mastroianni the icon, there was Mastroianni the dreamer. Luchino Visconti — the master behind The Leopard and Death in Venice — took a Dostoevsky short story and turned it into one of the most achingly romantic films of the 1950s. Shot entirely on hauntingly artificial, fog-soaked soundstages, White Nights follows a lonely young man who falls for a mysterious woman he meets on a bridge, across four unforgettable nights that blur the line between love and delusion. It's gorgeous. It's melancholic. It's Mastroianni at his most vulnerable, opposite a luminous Maria Schell — and it's the kind of film that doesn't get a big-screen showing very often. This is a rare chance to see it the way it was meant to be seen: on a real screen, in a real theater, with other people who love cinema as much as you do. Title: The Sensory Studio: Creative Exploration
Categories: Art Centers; Kids & Family Friendly; Lectures & Workshops; Visual Arts
Description: The Sensory Studio: Creative Exploration is a neurodivergent-friendly creative environment designed for exploration, regulation, and expressive making without pressure or expectation. This open studio experience offers a variety of art materials, such as clay, paint, drawing tools, collage, and tactile sensory elements… inviting children to engage in whatever way feels most comfortable for their bodies and nervous systems. Rather than following a single required project, students are offered gentle invitations and optional creative prompts alongside completely open-ended making time. Some children may choose to follow a simple guided idea, while others may prefer to experiment freely, focus on sensory engagement, or move between materials at their own pace. This class honors different communication styles, attention needs, and sensory experiences. The emphasis is not on finished artwork, but on process, comfort, and creative self-expression. Guided instruction will support the process while leaving plenty of room for imagination and personal interpretation. A playful, storybook-style class where Halloween meets winter magic through hands-on sculpting, creativity, and character-making in clay. Additional $10 material fee. Ages 6-12.

Title: Scott Keo: #1 Michael Bublé Tribute Worldwide
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: Scott has been bringing that amazing big band smooth “feel” to every event he and his swinging band have performed for, around the world! No cheese, no gimmicks. Just pure 1963 Sinatra Big Band vibe, with a unique, modern BUBLE’ punch. And, of course the voice. Can’t get Bublé sound without that velvet, buttery voice! Scott Keo, a southern California native, is a veteran of the music industry as both a premier Michael Bublé tribute act and an experienced wedding DJ. Over the past 15 years, Scott Keo has become known for his distinctive voice and entertaining performances. He has performed at thousands of weddings and special events throughout the U.S. Scott recorded and released his original song, “All To You” in 2010, which has sold over 14,000 copies to date and has acquired over 750,000 views on YouTube. Additionally, it has become extremely popular in the wedding world and was listed as a “Groom-Mother Dance” song by Wedding Wire, a popular wedding website. “I remember hearing Michael Bublé’s song “Home” and just being overwhelmed with the emotion he evokes with the lyrics and the tone of his voice,” Scott said. “I started using more Bublé songs in my wedding sets and becoming a bigger fan which let me to experiment with my own performance of his songs.” In 2011, Scott began his Michael Bublé Tribute Act impressing audiences everywhere with his unbelievable accuracy, energy and crowd involvement. As both a solo act and a tribute performer, Keo has had the pleasure of sharing the stage with Bob Caudle, Terry Davies, Dave Halstrom, Mike Martis, Peter Petty and Steve Roman.

Description: @ We all know learning is more fun when you’re drinking with friends. Title: A Christmas Story
Organization: DelawareScene (Div. of the Arts events portal)
Description: A Christmas Story Book by Joseph Robinette Music & Lyrics by Benj Pasek & Justin Paul Directed by John Hulse November 27 – December 20, 2026 You’ll shoot your eye out! Unwrap a holiday classic, just like it was the first time. Adapted from the original movie by the composers of La La Land, The Greatest Showman, and, yes, Dear Evan Hansen, this stage musical delighted Clear Space audiences years ago – and is back for a second helping. Ralphie’s got one Christmas wish: a Red Ryder BB gun with a compass in the stock and this thing that tells time. But, with a dreaded double-dog dare, a bunny suit, a Cracker Jack prize, and a very grumpy Santa, will he make it til December 25? Relive all the nostalgic holiday fun of the movie… with some new laughs, a big heart, and just the right amount of leg lamp glow to remind you that even if they’re wildly imperfect, our families are who make the holidays special.
